research_conclusion: Bounded cost-sensitivity check, independently verified. Under the repository's existing realistic and 2x conservative cost models with a cost-matched coin-flip null, the short-horizon momentum edge (lookback 3/5/10) is COST_ROBUST for the same 6/10 assets (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA), with 0 COST_ELIMINATED and 0 COST_ERODED; the robust-edge count is unchanged at 6/10 from zero to conservative cost. Candidate segment medians are essentially cost-invariant. MATERIAL QUALIFICATION: the cost model is not a conservative stress for this signal because the signal is nearly always long (9/10 assets ~4460 long / 0 short bars, 1 flip; only NVDA has short exposure), so it behaves like a constant-notional buy-and-hold with low effective turnover, and the engine adds slippage to buys and sells in the same (+price) direction so it cancels. Total conservative-level cost is small for the six COST_ROBUST assets (~$21k-$102k over 17 years on $1M); NVDA's cost is large (~$713k) but NVDA is NO_EDGE. Therefore the result is cost-robust under the existing model but is not evidence of survival under a directionally-correct conservative cost model, and it exposes a drift/long-bias confound that the symmetric coin-flip null does not control for. Verification: 4 independent gates MATCH (fresh walk_forward + noise_benchmark recomputation; zero-cost cross-consistency with the prior lookback sweep; verdict/classification re-derivation; turnover recompute + determinism); 168/168 regression tests pass.
